deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 1974 'topologie modérée' notes. The contexts are named on the previous page as L.P.M., S.A.P.M., Alg_C and An_C; the abbreviations are not expanded on this page. Grothendieck studies 'admissible partitions' (F_i)_{i∈I} of a space X. These are locally finite partitions into locally closed pieces, with connectedness required. They satisfy the frontier condition: each closure F̄_i is a union of pieces, equivalently F̄_j ∩ F_i ≠ ∅ ⇒ F_i ⊂ F̄_j. The index set I is ordered by i ≤ j iff F̄_i ⊂ F̄_j.

What this page serves: the previous page sets out to prove that a coarsest admissible partition exists and that its formation commutes with restriction to opens, reducing to local existence. So he needs to know how the order and the open pieces behave under restriction to an open U.

(1) Lemma. Fix an open U and i, j with F̄_i ∩ U ≠ ∅. This is equivalent to F_i ∩ U ≠ ∅, since U is open and F_i is dense in F̄_i. Claim: F̄_i ⊂ F̄_j ⇔ F̄_i ∩ U ⊂ F̄_j ∩ U.
- '⇒' is trivial.
- '⇐': take x ∈ F_i ∩ U. Near x we have F̄_i ⊂ F̄_j, so near x the set F̄_i ∩ F̄_j = ∪_{k∈K} F̄_k equals F̄_i.
- Each such F̄_k ⊂ F̄_i coincides with F̄_i near x. Does that force equality everywhere? 'Yes, since F_k is open in F̄_i', together with connectedness and the frontier condition.
- Hence F̄_i = F̄_k ⊂ F̄_j.
- Conclusion: on I_U = {i : F̄_i ∩ U ≠ ∅}, the order computed in U coincides with the order induced from I.

(2) Corollary. If F_i ∩ U ≠ ∅, then F_i is open in X ⇔ F_i ∩ U is open in U. Equivalently, i is maximal in I ⇔ i is maximal in I_U, using the next page's fact that F_i is open iff i is maximal.
- '⇒' is trivial.
- '⇐': let i be maximal in I_U and j ≥ i. Then F̄_j ⊃ F̄_i meets U, so j ∈ I_U, hence j = i.

(3) Section III starts a second formalism: stratifications given by a filtration.
- X = X^0 ⊃ X^1 ⊃ X^2 ⊃ … is a locally finite filtration by closed subsets.
- Each X^{i+1} is nowhere dense ('rare') in X^i, so X^{i+1} = X^i ⇔ X^i = ∅.
- Strata are V^i = X^i − X^{i+1}.
- Required conditions: for every open U, the connected components of U ∩ V^i form a locally finite family on U. For every component Z_α of U ∩ V^i, the set Z̄_α ∩ U ∩ V^j is open in U ∩ V^j.
- That is, the components of the V^i ∩ U satisfy the frontier condition, stably under restriction to opens.
- Margin: 'this is in fact a local condition; one may restrict to germs at x, for all x ∈ X'.

The next page shows Grothendieck noticing that connectedness of leaves is not stable under restriction. He then replaces it by the stable condition (C) on connected components of U ∩ F_i, which is the same idea as section III here.
errors: Index slips in section III. Grothendieck writes 'X^{i-1} rare dans X^i' and V^i = X^i − X^{i-1}; with a decreasing filtration this should read X^{i+1} rare in X^i and V^i = X^i − X^{i+1}. Likewise 'X^{i-1}=X^i ⇔ X^i=∅' should be 'X^{i+1}=X^i ⇔ X^i=∅'.
In the condition he writes '∀ i ∈ I' where the filtration index (i ∈ ℕ) is meant.

Gap in the lemma: the step 'equality near x ⇒ equality everywhere' needs connectedness of F_i, or the frontier condition applied to F_i ⊂ F̄_k. The connectedness of F_i ∩ U is not stable under restriction, which Grothendieck himself notices on the next page. With the frontier condition the argument is correct: x ∈ F_i ∩ F̄_k gives F_i ⊂ F̄_k, hence F̄_k = F̄_i.

ideas.what: The poset of strata (order by inclusion of closures) is compatible with restriction to opens, and openness or maximality of a stratum is a local property.
ideas.modern_name: Frontier condition; poset of strata of a stratification; locality of the stratification poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney (1965), Thom (1969), Mather (1970); standard in stratification theory
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 discusses tame topology and stratified structures only in general terms

ideas.what: Admissible partitions with connectedness replaced by a condition on connected components of U ∩ F_i for all opens U, so as to be local and stable under restriction (germ-wise condition).
ideas.modern_name: Locally defined (sheaf-like) stratifications; frontier condition imposed on connected components
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lojasiewicz / Hironaka (semi-analytic and subanalytic stratifications); o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries)
ideas.where_published: Possibly echoed in Esquisse d'un programme §5 ('stratifications modérées'); not in detail

ideas.what: Stratification presented by a locally finite decreasing filtration by closed nowhere-dense subsets, with conditions on the components of the differences.
ideas.modern_name: Filtered space / stratification by a filtration (e.g. Goresky–MacPherson style filtrations, Thom–Mather)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather; Goresky–MacPherson (1980) for the filtration formalism in intersection homology
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions filtrations of tame spaces in passing

deep.surprise_reason: Routine point-set lemmas on the frontier condition and its locality, preparatory to proving existence of a coarsest admissible partition. This is all standard in stratification theory; the only interest is documentary, showing Grothendieck's 1974 groundwork for 'topologie modérée'.
transcription_corrections: Section III indices are as written ('X^{i-1} rare dans X^i', 'V^i = X^i − X^{i-1}'). Grothendieck's own slip; mathematically X^{i+1} is meant.
'Oui, car F_k est ouvert[?] dans F̄_i' — 'ouvert' (underlined) appears to be the right reading.
The margin note reads approximately: 'C'est en fait une condition locale, on peut se borner à des germes en x, ∀ x ∈ X'.
